item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 18:27 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 18:27 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure. Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth, a small nodule, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early. The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant. "Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained." "The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days." A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking. "Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign," said Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital. "When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so, based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis," he said. LEO A RELATIVELY YOUNG POPE, PLAYS SPORTS Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well. "I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement. "The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it (today) ...are reassuring," Meloni added. The late Pope Francis, Leo's predecessor, died at age 88. He was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years. He did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health. The Vatican press office said Leo's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health. Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17. Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake."

item.content:encoded:
Germany backs Ukraine's Zelenskiy after Trump's call for his removal Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 18:20 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 18:20 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Sunday following US President Donald Trump's call for his removal and urged more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks. Wadephul said Germany remained by the side of Ukraine and its government "and fully support the President as he carries out his difficult duties." The comments, at a leadership meeting of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), followed Trump's call on Saturday for Zelenskiy to be replaced and underlined Berlin's growing rift with Washington. Trump, who last week announced a diesel supply deal with Russia, called for Ukraine to replace Zelenskiy and railed against Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure. Germany, the biggest European donor to Ukraine, said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia despite Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel. Wadephul, who met his Russian counterpart Sergei Lavrov on the margins of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month, said "consistency and clarity" were needed to support Ukraine and bring Moscow to negotiate. "We don't need less pressure, we need more pressure on Putin to make him be ready to negotiate," Wadephul said. "That is what this moment requires and that's what the government stands for." British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke with Zelenskiy on Saturday and told him the UK would continue to strengthen its sanctions on Russia, a Downing Street spokesperson said.

item.content:encoded:
Deutsche Bank chief warns German election results worrying foreign investors Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 18:13 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 18:13 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The head of Germany's largest bank warned that foreign investors may be driven away following victories in state elections last month by parties on the political extremes. The AfD, which wants to restrict immigration and send asylum seekers home, scored some of its biggest-ever wins in eastern Germany last month. At the same time, the Left Party scored its biggest win in the election for the city government of Berlin, pledging to expropriate holdings of property companies. "This poses a significant risk to Germany, and it should not be played down," Christian Sewing, chief executive of Deutsche Bank, told the Bild daily in an interview, referring to the rise of political extremes. "You can't expect a foreign investor to immediately draw a distinction between a state government and Germany as a whole," he said. "It's seen as Germany as a whole and I think that from an investor's point of view, that's understandable." In the state of Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD, which is classified by security services as extremist in some regions, only narrowly fell short of an absolute majority in the state parliament, and it followed up two weeks later by taking first place in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The AfD has been accused by economists of fostering a climate that will drive away badly needed skilled workers and foreign investors. The Left Party, meanwhile, vowed to tackle Berlin's soaring housing costs by expropriating the holdings of residential property companies. "And whether it's Saxony-Anhalt with the AfD or what's happening here in Berlin, it's anything but conducive to economic growth. And it's anything but investment-friendly," Sewing said. He urged the government of Chancellor Friedrich Merz to carry on with reforms to revive the economy. "That is the only response we have to the far-right and far-left extremists in this country," he said.
